items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the highway law, in relation to dedicating a portion of the
state highway system in the town of Lewisboro, county of Westchester, to the
Reynolds family
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9446

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the highway law, in relation to dedicating a portion of
the state highway system in the town of Lewisboro, county of Westches-
ter, to the Reynolds family

 
PURPOSE:

To dedicate a portion of the state highway in the town of Lewisboro,
county of Westchester, to the Reynolds family.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one amends section 344-s of the highway law to outline the
designation of a portion of state route thirty-five to the Reynolds
family.

Section two outlines the role of the commissioner of transportation in
the signing and maintenance of the highway's dedicated portion.

Section three provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Reynolds family embodies Cross River, recognizing generations of
residents whose history and service are deeply interwoven with the
area's heritage. The family played a crucial role in establishing the
community and contributed to the founding of the Cross River Baptist
Church in 1789, following the American Revolution.

Born and raised in the Reynolds family home along Route 35, Lois
Reynolds remained devoted to her hometown through her leadership at the
Cross River Baptist Church, as well as service to the Lewisboro Seniors
as president. Civic engagement was at the forefront of her mission,
ultimately being inducted into the Westchester County Senior Hall of
Fame for her lasting impact on generations of residents. This roadway
honors not only Lois' legacy and years of extraordinary service, but
also honors the Reynolds family's centuries-long contributions to the
history, civic life, and continued spirit of the Cross River.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

A.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the highway law, in relation to dedicating a portion of the
state highway system in the town of Lewisboro, county of Westchester, to
Nathaniel Reynolds
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9446A

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the highway law, in relation to dedicating a portion of
the state highway system in the town of Lewisboro, county of Westches-
ter, to Nathaniel Reynolds

 
PURPOSE:

To dedicate a portion of the state highway in the town of Lewisboro,
county of Westchester, to Nathaniel Reynolds.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends section 344-s of the highway law to outline the desig-
nation of a portion of state route thirty-five to Nathaniel Reynolds.
Section 2 outlines the role of the commissioner of transportation in the
signing and maintenance of the highway's dedicated portion. Section 3
provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Reynolds family of Cross River traces its roots to 1754, when more
than 100 acres were deeded to the family, the same year Nathaniel
Reynolds was born. The family played an important role in the communi-
ty's agricultural, religious, and civic life.

Nathaniel Reynolds was the father of 12 children. In addition to manag-
ing his farm year-round, he worked at the tailoring trade in the winter
months. This skill served him well during the Revolutionary War, when he
was captured by the British in June 1779 and held as a prisoner on a
British ship until his release in October 1781.  According to family
lore, he tailored uniforms for British officers.

Lieutenant Reynolds was an enlisted man in Colonel Crane's Westchester
County Militia and fought in the Battle of White Plains and in the
Battle of Ridgefield. In civilian life, he served as Fence Viewer, and
the Cross River Baptist Church was organized in his home in 1789.  From
those early beginnings, the Reynolds family remained the backbone of
that church community until the death of Lois Reynolds at age 106 in
July 2025, the last direct descendant of the Reynold's family living in
Cross River.

Lieutenant Nathaniel Reynolds died in 1843 and is buried in Cross River
Cemetery.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

summary: Dedicates a portion of the state highway system constituting state route thirty-five, beginning at its intersection with state route one hundred twenty-one and continuing to its intersection with North Salem road, in the town of Lewisboro, county of Westchester, to Nathaniel Reynolds.
